hevc.windowsBody: Your Windows is missing the HEVC codec, so HEVC files use slow software decode. Installing Microsoft's HEVC Video Extension lets your GPU decode them — fixes 4K HEVC. Note: 8K HEVC is beyond most GPUs even with the codec.
hevc.linuxBody:
Your Linux Chromium is using software HEVC decode, which stutters on 4K+ files. To enable hardware decode, install your distro's VA-API drivers and restart FunSync:
# Ubuntu / Debian (Intel iGPU)
sudo apt install intel-media-va-driver mesa-va-drivers

# Ubuntu / Debian (AMD GPU)
sudo apt install mesa-va-drivers

# Ubuntu / Debian (NVIDIA, recent drivers)
sudo apt install nvidia-vaapi-driver

# Fedora
sudo dnf install libva-utils mesa-va-drivers-freeworld

# Arch
sudo pacman -S libva-utils intel-media-driver libva-mesa-driver
Note: 8K HEVC is beyond most GPUs even with hardware decode.
hevc.macosBody: Your macOS Chromium can't use VideoToolbox HEVC — this usually means you're on macOS 10.12 or older (HEVC requires 10.13+). Update macOS to enable hardware HEVC decode. Note: even on supported macOS, 8K HEVC needs an Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3) — older Intel Macs top out around 4K HEVC.
hevc.genericBody: HEVC files in your library will use slow software decode on this platform and may stutter, especially at 4K and above.

playback.rangeExtenderHint: When a script's stroke positions stay in a narrow range (e.g. 30–70), stretch them so they use the device's full range. Applies to all devices on next video load.
playback.rangeExtenderResetAria: Reset Stretch limited-range scripts to default
playback.rangeLivePreviewHint: With nothing playing, dragging a Range slider in the Connection panel moves the device to that limit, so you can see where it sits — useful after changing a sleeve. Position devices only; silent during playback.
playback.rangeLivePreviewResetAria: Reset Preview range on the device to default
playback.orgasmScriptHint: Hold X during playback to swap your device(s) onto this short looping script, then release to snap back. Works with Handy, Buttplug and T-Code.
playback.orgasmScriptHintToggle: Tap X during playback to put your device(s) on this short looping script, and tap X again to stop them. Works with Handy, Buttplug and T-Code.
playback.orgasmModeHint: Hold to ride: hold X to play the looping script, release to return to the main script. Press to finish: tap X to start it looping, tap again to stop the device — it won't return to the main script.
playback.orgasmPatternHint: Loops a generated pattern instead of a script file. Your script choice is kept for when you switch back.
playback.edgeModeToggle: Press to hold (press again to resume)
playback.edgeModeHint: Hold to edge: hold Z to stop your device(s) while the video keeps playing, release and the script picks back up in sync. Press to hold: tap Z to stop them, tap again to resume — easier on the hand during a long edge.
playback.globalHotkeysHint: These work even while FunSync is minimised or another app has focus, and a key set here stops reaching every other app. Click a box, then press a key with two of Ctrl, Alt and Shift, or F13–F24 or a media key on its own. Ctrl+Alt needs Shift too, because on many keyboards Ctrl+Alt is AltGr, which types characters such as @. Everyday shortcuts (copy, paste, undo, save…), F1–F12 with fewer than two modifiers, and the cursor and editing keys are refused. From a global hotkey, Orgasm Switch and Edge Hold always toggle (press to start, press again to stop).
playback.globalHotkeyNeedsModifier: {key} takes that key away from typing in every other app — try it with Ctrl+Alt+Shift
playback.globalHotkeyAppShortcut: {key} is a shortcut other apps use (copy, paste, undo, save, refresh…), and it stops working in all of them — try it with Ctrl+Alt+Shift, or use F13–F24
playback.globalHotkeyAltGr: On many keyboards Ctrl+Alt is AltGr, so {key} can stop a character such as @ or € typing in every app — add Shift
playback.globalHotkeyCursorKey: {key} is a cursor, editing or screenshot key that other apps use with every modifier — pick a letter, digit or F-key instead
playback.globalHotkeyNotActiveTaken: Not active: the system or another app already uses {key}. Pick a different hotkey.
playback.globalHotkeyNotActiveInvalid: Not active: {key} isn't a valid key combination. Pick a different hotkey.
playback.randomVariantHint: When a video has multiple script variations, pick one at random each time it plays. Overrides pinned default variations while on.
playback.bpHint: Per-stroke sends one command per action and lets the device's firmware interpolate — matches how the Handy's WiFi API (HSSP) feels. Lookahead compensates for BLE round-trip; min stroke stretches too-short strokes up so BLE can honor them. For Handy via connection code (HSSP), these have no effect.
playback.inlineVizPlacementHint: Under the video keeps the whole picture clear: the video gets a little smaller and the timeline and heatmap sit in a strip beneath it. Turn them on with TL and HM in the player. The opacity below is for over the video.
playback.inlineTimelineAnchorLeft: Near the left (more of what is coming)
playback.inlineTimelineHint: For the Timeline overlay (TL). A longer window shows more of the script at once. Near the left shows more of what is coming than of what has passed.
playback.deviceSimOpacityHint: How solid the stroke indicator looks over the video. Show it with the D key or from the player's ⋮ menu.
playback.deviceSimHint: In the player, drag the simulator to move it, drag its corner to resize it, drag the knob on its end to turn it, and right-click it for its direction and colour.
playback.inlineVizOpacityHint: How solid the script timeline and heatmap strip look over the video. Turn them on from the player's ⋮ menu.
playback.seekFrameStripLabel: Frame strip on the seek bar
playback.seekFrameStripHint: A row of frames from the video along the top of the seek bar, so you can see where to jump. Drawn from the video itself while you watch, a little at a time; local files only. Big VR videos take longer to fill.
playback.heatmapPlayheadHint: Draws a line on the heatmap strip at the current position, like the timeline's cursor. Turn the strip on from the player's ⋮ menu.
playback.smoothOverlaysHint: Off by default. Turns off Windows' DirectComposition for FunSync. Try it if the picture pauses for a moment every few seconds while the timeline, the heatmap marker or the device simulator is on screen. If other apps pause the same way, the cause is the PC (a driver or a background tool) and this will not help. Takes effect after restarting the app.
playback.smoothOverlaysRestart: Restart FunSync to apply the rendering change.
playback.rememberSpeedHint: Keep the current speed when you load another video. Off by default, so each video starts at 1x.
playback.openFullscreenHint: Start in fullscreen when you play a video from the library. Escape leaves fullscreen as usual.
playback.autoplayOnOpenHint: Play straight away when you open a video from the library, instead of loading it paused. Off by default, so a single click never starts a device moving on its own.
playback.autoplayOnOpenResetAria: Reset Start playing on open to default
playback.fillerPreviewAria: Preview of the filler stroke pattern
playback.fillerHint: Plays gentle strokes during long blank stretches of script instead of leaving the device still. Ignored when Gap Skip is set to automatic.
playback.orgasmLibraryHint: Loops a pattern from the built-in library instead of a script file. Your script choice is kept for when you switch back.
playback.edgeActionHint: Stop the devices: they rest while the video plays on. Play a pattern: they play the pattern below instead, even while the video is paused. Either way, when the hold ends the script picks back up in sync; on a paused video it waits until you press play.
playback.patternRangeWidened: This range is too narrow for the pattern, so it plays a little wider: {lo} to {hi}.
playback.orgasmLibraryNone: No pattern chosen yet. Until you choose one, X plays your script file as before.
playback.edgePatternNone: No pattern chosen yet, so Z stops the devices, as with "Stop the devices". Choose a pattern above.
playback.fillerResetThresholdAria: Reset the gap filler threshold to its default (10s)
playback.edgeCarryLabel: Keep Z on into the next video
playback.edgeCarryHint: Off: a new video starts with Z off and its script plays. On: Z stays on when the next video starts (handy while a queue plays on), the device waits, and a note on the video says how to start the script.
playback.orgasmCarryLabel: Keep X on into the next video
playback.orgasmCarryHint: Off: a new video ends X and its script plays. On: the looping script keeps playing into the next video (handy while a queue plays on), that video's script waits, and a note on the video says how to end it.

appearance.themeHint: Choose how the app looks. "System" follows your OS preference and switches automatically when you toggle dark / light at the OS level.
appearance.styleHint: Keep the classic look, switch to a modern style with more depth and polish, or go festive with Holiday. Classic and Modern use the same colours.
appearance.styleHolidayDesc: Festive colours, the logo in a Santa hat, and a little snow. Works with Dark and Light.
appearance.holidaySnowHint: A few slow snowflakes. Never over a video, and off when your system asks for less motion.
appearance.scaleHint: Makes everything in the main window larger or smaller. Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- change it too, and Ctrl+0 goes back to 100%. While a VR video is open, those keys zoom the video instead.
appearance.languageHint: Switch the interface language. Changes apply immediately.
appearance.movingPreviewsHint: Play a short video preview when you hover over a library item. Turn off to speed up browsing on large libraries — static thumbnails are still shown.
appearance.folderPreviewsHint: Show a mosaic of the videos inside on folder tiles. Turn off to use a plain folder icon instead.
appearance.miniPlayerHint: When you go back to the library while a video is playing, it shrinks into a corner mini-player and keeps playing (and keeps driving your device) instead of stopping.
appearance.hwDecodeHint: On by default. If videos won't play — a black screen or decode error, common on NVIDIA + Linux — turn this off to use software decoding. Takes effect after restarting the app.
appearance.hwDecodeRestart: Restart FunSync to apply the video decoding change.
appearance.cardHeatmapHint: Show a stroke-speed heatmap under each thumbnail. Uses the video's main script. Off by default because it reads a script per card.
appearance.tagsOnCardsHint: Show a few of each video's tags under its name. The video's options (⋮, then Tags) list them all.
appearance.resumeProgressHint: Show how far through each video you got, as a bar on playlist cards and rows. Playlist playback only — the main library is left unmarked.
appearance.hideDupesHint: Show only one entry when several videos share an identical filename, such as the same file in two source folders. The copy with a script is kept.
appearance.folderScriptsAsVariantsLabel: One-video folders: offer every script in the folder as a variant
appearance.folderScriptsAsVariantsHint: For journeys and FapLand rounds: when a folder holds just one video, every other script in it is offered in that video's script menu, on the phone too. Its own script stays the default and axis files stay axis files. Nothing on disk changes, so turning this off simply stops offering them.
appearance.navHint: Untick a button to hide it from the bar. Library and Settings always stay. The H key still opens Devices, but Web Remote and VR have no other way in, so tick them again when you need them.

data.backupBlurb: Your settings are automatically backed up every minute while you use the app and before any destructive change. If something goes wrong you can restore an earlier state.

data.restoreConfirmBody: Your current settings will be saved as an emergency snapshot first, so you can undo if needed. The app will relaunch to apply the restored state.
data.exportBlurb: Save your settings, playlists, categories, associations and custom thumbnails to a portable file — useful for moving to another machine or for an extra off-host backup.
data.exportDialogBody: Saves your playlists, categories, tags, associations and settings to one file, to restore later or on another PC.
data.exportSecretsHint: Your Handy key, Autoblow token, EroScripts login and Audience keys. Not recommended: anyone who has the file can use them. Left out, you enter them again after restoring on another PC.
data.importConfirmBody: Choose a FunSync backup file next. Its playlists, categories and associations are added to yours (a playlist you already have is kept as it is, except Favourites, which gets the backup's favourites added), and its settings replace your current ones. Keys and logins you already have here are kept. Playback and every device stop first. Your current state is saved as a snapshot, so Restore From Backup can undo this. The app will relaunch to load the result.

vrModal.title: VR
vrModal.experimentalText: VR streaming and device sync are still being tuned. Expect rough edges around reconnection, sync timing, and player-specific quirks.
vrModal.streamingIntro: Set up HereSphere to browse and stream FunSync's library directly. No file transfers — works on Quest standalone or PCVR.
vrModal.hsUrlHint: Type this into the URL bar at the top of HereSphere's home screen on your Quest.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep2: Type the URL above into HereSphere's URL bar (at the top of the home screen) and press Enter.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep3: Your FunSync library appears — pick a video to play.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep4: Optional: bookmark or favourite the page in HereSphere so you don't have to retype next time.
vrModal.setupSyncStep2: Enable the timestamp server — required for FunSync to drive non-Handy devices.
vrModal.setupSyncStep3: Check that the IP field shows your Quest's current IP. If it's blank or stale (e.g. your Quest got a new IP since you set this up), press the auto-find button next to the IP field — HereSphere fills it in for you. Port should be 23554.
vrModal.setupSyncStep4: FunSync auto-detects your Quest and connects when you open a video in HereSphere.
vrModal.setupTrUrlBar: URL bar not visible? It's at the top of HereSphere's home screen — tap the address area to bring up the keyboard.
vrModal.setupTrNoVideos: No videos showing? Make sure FunSync is open with at least one source added.
vrModal.setupTrUnreachable: FunSync shows "VR companion can't reach HereSphere's timestamp server", or only the Handy moves while other devices stay silent? HereSphere isn't accepting connections on the address FunSync is reaching for. Two common fixes, in order:
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableStep1: Press the auto-find button next to the IP field in HereSphere's Timestamp Server settings — captures your Quest's current local IP. Useful when the IP has changed since setup (DHCP lease renewed, new router, etc.).
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableStep2: Toggle the timestamp server off and back on — clears any stuck state. HereSphere has had bugs in older versions where the listener didn't re-initialise after switching profiles; toggling fixes that.
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableTail: As a last resort, manually type the Quest's IP and port 23554 into the fields — same end result, less convenient.
vrModal.setupTrWaiting: Nav-bar VR icon yellow / status reads "Waiting"? TCP is connected but HereSphere isn't sending timestamp packets. Most often this means no video is playing in HereSphere — start one and the status flips to green within a second. If it stays yellow while a video is playing, toggle the timestamp server off and on in HereSphere to force a re-init.
vrModal.setupTrNoConnect: Can't connect at all? Make sure your Quest and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network.
vrModal.setupTrVpn: VPN active? Disable it — VPNs change your network IP and block local connections.
vrModal.setupTrProjection: Video looks wrong? Adjust projection mode in HereSphere (SBS, fisheye, etc.).
vrModal.syncIntro: Connect FunSync to HereSphere so devices follow playback. Works on Quest standalone, Quest Link, or PCVR.
vrModal.statusWaiting: Waiting for HereSphere to send timestamps. Check 'Timestamp Server' is on.

tip-strokes-slow-up-quick-down.name: Tip strokes, slow up, quick down

frantic-tip-strokes.name: Frantic tip strokes
frantic-tip-strokes.desc: Flat-out half-length strokes up at the tip.

tip-strokes-long-short.name: Tip strokes, long-short
tip-strokes-long-short.desc: Steady half-length strokes at the tip: a long stroke, then one about half as deep.

tip-strokes-slow-quick.name: Tip strokes, slow-quick pairs

frantic-tip-strokes-top-dip.name: Frantic tip strokes, dip at the top
frantic-tip-strokes-top-dip.desc: Flat-out half-length strokes at the tip, each long stroke followed by a little dip at the top.

fast-base-strokes.name: Fast base strokes
fast-base-strokes.desc: Fast half-length strokes down at the base, staying deep.

uneven-base-strokes.name: Uneven base strokes
uneven-base-strokes.desc: Brisk short strokes at the base whose timing and depth wander and never quite repeat.

slow-base-grind.name: Slow base grind
slow-base-grind.desc: A slow, tight grind right down at the base, slow up and quick down.

base-strokes-slow-up-quick-down.name: Base strokes, slow up, quick down
base-strokes-slow-up-quick-down.desc: Brisk half-length strokes at the base, slow up and quick down.

fast-base-strokes-long-short.name: Fast base strokes, long-short
fast-base-strokes-long-short.desc: Fast half-length strokes at the base: a long stroke, then a shorter one that turns back before the top.

frantic-base-grind.name: Frantic base grind
frantic-base-grind.desc: A flat-out, tight grind right down at the base, slow up and quick down.

base-strokes-high-low.name: Base strokes, high-low pairs
base-strokes-high-low.desc: Brisk half-length strokes at the base: one reaching up high, the next one lower.

frantic-base-strokes-bottom-bump.name: Frantic base strokes, bump at the bottom
frantic-base-strokes-bottom-bump.desc: Flat-out half-length strokes at the base, each long stroke followed by a little bump at the bottom.

buzz-uneven-short-base-strokes.name: Buzz on uneven short base strokes
buzz-uneven-short-base-strokes.desc: Uneven, brisk short strokes at the base with a buzz over most of them.

buzz-uneven-half-base-strokes.name: Buzz on uneven half base strokes
buzz-uneven-half-base-strokes.desc: Uneven, steady half-length strokes at the base with a buzz over most of them.

buzz-uneven-long-strokes.name: Buzz on uneven long strokes
buzz-uneven-long-strokes.desc: Uneven, fast long strokes through the middle with a buzz over most of them.

steady-buzz-base.name: Steady buzz at the base
steady-buzz-base.desc: A vibration at the base that stays put, with no real strokes under it.

buzz-long-strokes.name: Buzz on long strokes
buzz-long-strokes.desc: Steady long strokes through the middle with a buzz laid over them.

steady-buzz-tip-high.name: Steady buzz at the tip, high
steady-buzz-tip-high.desc: A vibration high up at the tip that stays put, with no real strokes under it.

buzz-frantic-base-strokes.name: Buzz on frantic base strokes
buzz-frantic-base-strokes.desc: Uneven, flat-out short strokes at the base with a buzz over most of them.

buzz-uneven-tip-strokes.name: Buzz on uneven tip strokes
buzz-uneven-tip-strokes.desc: Uneven, steady half-length strokes at the tip with a buzz over most of them.

buzz-tiny-base-strokes.name: Buzz on tiny base strokes
buzz-tiny-base-strokes.desc: Tiny flat-out strokes at the base with a buzz laid over them.

steady-buzz-tip-low.name: Steady buzz at the tip, lower
steady-buzz-tip-low.desc: A vibration lower down at the tip that stays put, with no real strokes under it.

buzz-short-tip-strokes.name: Buzz on short tip strokes
buzz-short-tip-strokes.desc: Short flat-out strokes at the tip with a buzz laid over them.

climbing-long-strokes.name: Climbing long strokes
climbing-long-strokes.desc: Fast long strokes that start midway and work their way up toward the tip.

sinking-full-strokes.name: Sinking full strokes
sinking-full-strokes.desc: Slow strokes that start midway and work their way down toward the base.

climbing-half-strokes-from-low.name: Climbing half strokes from low
climbing-half-strokes-from-low.desc: Flat-out half-length strokes that start low and work their way up toward the tip.

ladder-stepping-up.name: Ladder, stepping up
ladder-stepping-up.desc: Steady strokes whose bottom steps up a level each time, then it starts again.

pause-at-top.desc: Comes up, waits near the tip for about two seconds, then heads back down.

pause-at-bottom.name: Pause at the bottom
pause-at-bottom.desc: Rests right down at the base for about two seconds before the next stroke up.

pause-halfway.name: Pause halfway
pause-halfway.desc: Freezes halfway along a stroke for about two seconds, then carries on.

dip-climb-hold-top.name: Dip, climb back, hold at the top
dip-climb-hold-top.desc: A dip, a slow climb back up to the tip, then a wait of a couple of seconds.

fading-long-strokes-bottoms-rising.name: Fading long strokes, bottoms rising
fading-long-strokes-bottoms-rising.desc: Brisk long strokes that get shorter and quicker as the bottoms come up.

swelling-long-strokes-deeper.name: Swelling long strokes, reaching deeper
swelling-long-strokes-deeper.desc: Steady long strokes that get longer as the bottoms reach deeper.

slowing-full-strokes.name: Slowing full strokes
slowing-full-strokes.desc: Steady strokes the whole length that slow down as they go.

swelling-long-strokes-higher.name: Swelling long strokes, reaching higher

fading-long-strokes-tops-falling.name: Fading long strokes, tops falling
fading-long-strokes-tops-falling.desc: Brisk long strokes that get shorter and quicker as the tops come down.

speeding-up-low-strokes.desc: Brisk long strokes low down that speed up as they go, slow up and quick down.

fading-half-strokes-tops-falling.name: Fading half strokes, tops falling

stuttering-tip-strokes.name: Stuttering strokes at the tip

stuttering-base-strokes.name: Stuttering strokes at the base
stuttering-base-strokes.desc: Brisk short strokes at the base that keep catching, with little twitches back.

mixed-flutters-tip.name: Mixed flutters at the tip
mixed-flutters-tip.desc: Little flutters mixed with bigger, slower moves at the tip, gentle and never regular.

long-strokes-catch-up.name: Long strokes, catch on the way up
long-strokes-catch-up.desc: Steady long strokes that slip back a little partway up, then carry on to the top.

full-strokes-stall-down.name: Full strokes, stall on the way down
full-strokes-stall-down.desc: Brisk strokes the whole length that stop for a moment on the way down.

fast-full-strokes-catch-up.name: Fast full strokes, catch on the way up
fast-full-strokes-catch-up.desc: Fast strokes the whole length that slip back a little partway up, slow up and quick down.

half-strokes-catch-down.name: Half strokes, catch on the way down

long-strokes-stall-up.name: Long strokes, stall on the way up
long-strokes-stall-up.desc: Steady long strokes that stop for a moment on the way up: a slow stroke, then a quick one.

last-stroke-then-still.name: Last stroke down, then still
last-stroke-then-still.desc: The strokes stop: one last stroke down to the bottom, and it stays there.

slow-down-finish.name: Slow-down to the finish
slow-down-finish.desc: The strokes keep going but ease off, slower and slower until they stop.

sprint-finish.name: Sprint to the end
sprint-finish.desc: Faster than before and kept up right to the end, then it stops.

plunge-finish.name: The plunge
plunge-finish.desc: One last fast drop from up high all the way down, and it stays down.

buzz-finish.name: Buzz finish
buzz-finish.desc: The last stretch turns into mostly vibration instead of strokes.

finishing-fast-strokes-long-short.name: Finishing fast strokes, long-short
finishing-fast-strokes-long-short.desc: Fast strokes the whole length: a long stroke, then a shorter one, slow up and quick down.

full-strokes-base-flutter.name: Full strokes, flutter at the base
full-strokes-base-flutter.desc: Big strokes that hit the bottom, flutter there for a moment, then go straight back up.

drop-buzzing-aftershocks.name: Drop, then buzzing aftershocks
drop-buzzing-aftershocks.desc: The strokes come down to the bottom and keep buzzing and twitching there for a few seconds.

fast-strokes-flutter-both-ends.name: Fast strokes, flutter at both ends
fast-strokes-flutter-both-ends.desc: Quick strokes that flutter at the top, shoot down, flutter at the bottom and shoot back up.

fast-full-strokes-long-short-bottom.name: Fast full strokes, long-short from the bottom
fast-full-strokes-long-short-bottom.desc: Fast strokes the whole length: a long stroke, then one about half as deep that turns back before the top.

frantic-base-strokes-long-short.name: Frantic base strokes, long-short

live.syncedGone: Synced. {name} is gone from Stash; its data is kept.
live.syncedChanged: Synced. This file still differs from the one matched; its Stash data stays hidden.
live.relinked: This file is now linked to {name}.
live.noneOfThese: None of these scenes will be offered for this file again.
live.ignored: That Stash scene will not be offered for this file again.
live.undoFailed: Can't undo: FunSync could not change its Stash data.
live.refusedLinkChanged: It is now linked to {name}, which was left as it is.

error.fileOffline: FunSync could not read this video's file (its drive may be offline). Nothing was changed.
error.busy: Stash is syncing already. Try again when it ends.
error.changedMeanwhile: This video's Stash data changed meanwhile. Nothing was changed.
error.saveFailed: FunSync could not save its Stash data. Nothing was changed.
error.generic: Stash could not be asked. Nothing was changed.

stash.sceneChanged: The Stash scene with this id no longer has this file (Stash may have been reset or rescanned). Its data is hidden. Unlink it, or link it again with Find in Stash…

error.unreachable: Can't reach Stash at {address}. Is it running?
error.timeout: Stash did not answer in time.
error.badKey: Stash refused the API key. If your Stash has no password, remove the key.
error.needsKey: This Stash has a password. Paste its API key (Stash: Settings > Security).
error.forbidden: Stash refused this computer. Set a password in Stash and paste its API key.
error.tooOld: This Stash ({version}) is too old. FunSync needs v{minVersion} or newer.
error.tooOldNoVersion: This Stash is too old. FunSync needs v{minVersion} or newer.
error.notStash: That address answered, but not as Stash.
error.redirect: Stash sent FunSync to another address, which FunSync does not follow. Check the address.
error.certificate: This computer does not trust Stash's https certificate. Check the address.
error.graphql: Stash could not answer FunSync's request.
error.tooLarge: Stash's answer was too large to read.
error.badAddress: Enter an address that starts with http:// or https://, like http://127.0.0.1:9999.
error.badInput: FunSync could not send that request to Stash.
error.invalidKey: That is not a Stash API key. Copy it from Stash: Settings > Security > API Key.
error.writeFailed: FunSync could not save the API key. It is kept until FunSync closes.
error.removeFailed: FunSync could not remove the saved API key file.
error.keyUnreadable: The saved API key can't be read on this computer. Paste it again.
